refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: This program computes and output scaler sums from event files. The output files can include scaler labels provided from the file specified by --name-file or can be without labels (if scalers are 32 bits wide, see NAME FILE FORMAT below). The orientation of the output can either be one scaler per row and one file per column or it can be one scaler per column, one row per input file (if --flip is specified).

Output files are essentially comma separated fields (CSV) and therefore can be easily imported to e.g. Excel worksheets. Note, however that the quoting of labels is rather done in a primitive manner and does not support embedded quotation marks. For example a scaler lable like: Detector 1" above beam axis will get rendered as "Detector 1" above beam axis" which is incorrect, so take care when choosing scaler labels (e.g in the above you might use Detector 1 inch above beam axis or perhaps even better Detector 2.54cm above beam axis).

refsect1.title: NAME FILE FORMAT
refsect1.para: The --name-file option allows you to supply a file containing scaler label information. The format of this file is not the same as the scaler definition file that the scaler display requires. See, however makeNameFile (next reference page).
The name file format describes each scaler channel, one-per-line. Each line contains four fields that are space separated these contain on order

listitem.para: The original source id of the scaler channel. Note that prior to NSCLDAQ-12, the rewrites of the body header performed by glom, lost information about the original source id. This information is retained in the bodies of NSCLDAQ-12 and later scaler ring items. This value should refer to this original source id.
Note that when event building is not used, this is normally (though it need not be) zero.
The channel number of the scaler item within its data source. This is the uint32_t offset at which that channel appears in the array of scalers read for that data source. Offsets are numbered from 0.

Since there are still a few CAMAC systems in use and scalers from those systems are 24 bits wide and may contain bits set in their top 8 bits, this provides the bit-width of the scaler channel. This should normally be either 32 or 24 (CAMAC). Note, however the software supports any bit width between 1 and 32. Wider scalers are not supported in NSCLDAQ as each scaler item in a ring item is 32 bits wide.
The label that identifies the scaler.

refsect1.para: Note that if a scaler label is not provided for a scaler that appears in the data, the scaler will be labeled with its sourceid and channel number.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Create name file for scalersum from ScalerDisplay file

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: See the previous man page (scalersum). This utility script reads a scaler display definition file (def-file) and writes scalersum scaler name file (name-file).

refnamediv.refpurpose: Make name files from pyScaler TOML definition files.

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para:
This command makes a name file for the
program using, as input, the TOML configuration file for the program.
pyscalerdef-toml is the path to the pyScalers TOML configuration file. output-file is the path to where the scalersum scaler name file should be written.

note.title: NOTE
note.para: If you have scaler sources with source ids other than 0, you must add a sourceid specification to data sources for which that's true. This is ignored by pyScaler but provides the source id for the data source to write into the name file for each scaler from that source.

example.title: Sample data source with source id
example.programlisting: [datasource.testing] url='tcp://spdaq20/ron' version=12 scalers=['triggers.live', 'sin1', 'sin2', 'sin3', 'sin4', 'sin5', 'sin6', 'sin7', 'sin8', 'sin9', 'sin10', 'triggers.raw'] incremental = false sourceid=1

refsect1.para: The example above says that data from the ringbuffer ron in spdaq20 will have a source id of 1. If the sourceid definition is not provided, the source id defaults to 0
